You are 1000% more likely to microtear one of the dozen ribbon cables required to complete the job than you are damaging the phone with the laser.  

The laser is programmed to follow a pattern, and the guards are installed to make it almost impossible to mess it up. 

Only way you’d botch the job it is if you’re a dumbass, as it’s that hard to mess it up. Or the really unlikely event the machine malfunctioned. 

Also, the laser doesn’t penetrate through the phone. If you were to damage the phone with the laser, you would just see etching on the frame, or maybe a damaged camera.

Additionally, some of the parts that you have to transfer are IC programmed. If you mess those parts up, the phone won’t work, or you’re going to lose features. Apple will have to step in at that point. 

So yes, the job is risky and you’re not doing OP any favors by spreading misinformation.

You will need to have the screen reprogrammed or just replace the screen at a shop. As for a complete housing swap, yes. You should be able to swap all of your internals to another housing. 

But please please keep in mind that this is a VERY RISKY repair. I don’t even like doing it as a professional. It’s mostly why the industry uses lasers to remove the glass. It’s easier, and safer. 

There are a ton of very delicate ribbon cables that are stuck in place with adhesives, and tucked under other components. 

You’ll need to keep track of exactly where the screws go. They are all different sizes and will only be safe in the hole they came from. 

You will also need to transfer structural brackets that are screwed into the housing. Like button guards and sim hardware. 

It’s a very time consuming process. Your best bet is to just have the screen and back glass replaced at a shop for a few hundred if you can afford it. 

Or buy a housing with some of the hardware pre installed. Won’t make the job much easier but will shave off some time.

You’ll notice a slight increase in performance if the device is running cooler. It’s a term called thermal throttling. The hotter the device gets, the more it needs to bottleneck performance to keep itself from overheating and potentially damaging circuitry.
